summary: Four studies directly apply Bayesian hierarchical (multilevel probabilistic) models with partial pooling to fraud detection. [V0068] Brennan et al. (2018) evaluated on GridWatch, achieving F1=0.89. [V0067] Adebayo et al. (2026) evaluated on ToxiBench, achieving AUROC=0.82. [V0065] Gupta et al. (2024) evaluated on LedgerGuard, achieving accuracy=0.68. [V0066] Haddad et al. (2025) evaluated on CellLife, achieving MAE=0.75. These four are the core directly relevant documents. A fifth slot is filled by [V0019] Gupta et al. (2024), which applies the same multilevel probabilistic model with partial pooling but to septic deterioration prediction on LedgerGuard (accuracy=0.83); it is methodologically identical but applied to a different domain, making it the closest remaining candidate. Documents such as [V0116], [V0235], [V0162], and [V0043] apply the method to unrelated tasks (hate speech, traffic, protein function, agricultural yield) and are excluded. Documents [V0069], [V0058], [V0050], [V0052], [V0054], and [V0063] address fraud detection but use different methods (representation learning, decentralised training, graph message passing, self-attention, boosted trees) and are therefore not directly relevant to Bayesian hierarchical modelling. Documents [V0103], [V0141], [V0142], and [V0152] only mention multilevel probabilistic models as prior work and do not apply them.

claims.value: Multilevel probabilistic models with partial pooling (Bayesian hierarchical)

claims.attribute: Best reported F1 among Bayesian hierarchical fraud detection studies
Same method applied to septic deterioration (non-fraud, included as 5th candidate)
